questions.question: Who among the following is credited with single-handedly making the Santoor a popular classical instrument?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following is credited with single-handedly making the Santoor a popular classical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Shiv Kumar Sharma.

Key Points

  • Pandit Shivkumar Sharma was an Indian famous classical musician, who attained international fame by playing the musical instrument, the santoor.
  • The Santoor is a trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer often made of walnut wood and has 72 strings, which are struck with two delicate carved wooden mallets.
  • The santoor is essentially a folk instrument that originated in the Kashmir Valley, and it achieved the status of a classical instrument due to the persistent efforts and genius of Pandit Shivkumar Sharma.
  • With his hard work, determination and talent, Pandit Shivkumar Sharma made the santoor a global name. 

Additional Information

  • Pandit Bhajan Sopori was an Indian instrumentalist.
  • He was a player of the santoor, an ancient stringed musical instrument.
  • Rahul Sharma is an Indian music director and Indian classical santoor player. 
  • Pandit Ulhas Bapat was a santoor player from India.

questions.question: Which of the following instruments is normally played in a vertical position and with an arched bow?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following instruments is normally played in a vertical position and with an arched bow?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sarangi.

Key Points

Sarangi

  • It is also called saran or Saranga, short-necked fiddle used throughout South Asia, particularly for folk and classical Hindustani music. Measuring about 76 cm (30 inches) long, the instrument has a roughly rectangular slightly waisted body and broad fretless neck generally carved from a single piece of wood.
  • It has three melody strings made of gut, usually tuned a fifth and a fourth apart, and 11 to 37 sympathetically vibrating metal strings.
  • The musician, who is seated, normally holds the instrument against his left shoulder in a vertical position and plays with an arched bow held in an underhand grip in his right hand. Hence, Option 4 is correct.
  • The cuticles (or sometimes the space on the fingernail just above the cuticles) of the left hand are pressed against the strings to sound specific pitches.

​

Additional Information

Shehnai

  • It is double-reed conical oboe of North India.
  • The Shehnai is made of wood, except for a flaring metal bell attached to the bottom of the instrument, and measures about 12–20 inches (30–50 cm) in length, with six to eight keyless finger holes along its body.

Veena

  • It is among the oldest Indian musical instruments.
  • From the references to Vedic writings, it can date back to around the first millennium B.C. Temple sculptures from the 2nd century B.C. show a type of veena being played.
  • The Saraswati Veena is predominant in Carnatic music and the Rudra veena is the most played veena in Hindustani music.
  • The Saraswati veena has seven strings strung over twenty-four fixed frets.
  • It is played by sitting cross-legged, with the resonator to the player's right.
  • The veena is said to be the only instrument that can play all the Gamakas (oscillations) in Carnatic music, usually something that only the most proficient vocalists can achieve.
  • The Hindu Goddess of Knowledge, Saraswati, is said to play the Veena.
  • Pictures depict her sitting on a lotus and playing the instrument.

Sitar

  • It is a stringed instrument of the lute family that is popular in northern India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.
  • The instrument was invented in medieval India, flourished in the 16th and 17th centuries, and arrived at its present form in 18th-century India.
  • Used widely throughout the Indian subcontinent, the sitar became popularly known in the wider world through the works of Ravi Shankar, beginning in the late 1950s and early 1960s.

questions.question: KV Prasad, SV Rajarao, Umalayapuram Sivaraman, Palghat Mani Iyer, Karaikudi R Mani and Palghat Raghu are noted players of which of the following instruments?
questions.questionHtml: KV Prasad, SV Rajarao, Umalayapuram Sivaraman, Palghat Mani Iyer, Karaikudi R Mani and Palghat Raghu are noted players of which of the following instruments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mridangam.

Key Points

  • Mridangam is a classical percussion instrument from South India, widely used in Carnatic music.
  • Notable Mridangam players include KV Prasad, SV Rajarao, Umalayapuram Sivaraman, Palghat Mani Iyer, Karaikudi R Mani, and Palghat Raghu.
  • The Mridangam is an ancient instrument, with references dating back to ancient Indian scriptures and epics.
  • It is known for its deep and resonant sound, making it a fundamental component in South Indian classical performances.

Additional Information

  • Construction: The Mridangam is typically made from a hollowed piece of jackfruit wood, with animal skin stretched over both ends to create drumheads.
  • Playing Technique: It is played using fingers and palms, with each hand controlling a different drumhead to produce a variety of sounds.
  • Role in Music: In Carnatic music, the Mridangam provides rhythmic support and enhances the overall performance.
  • Training: Learning the Mridangam involves rigorous practice under the guidance of a guru, focusing on various rhythmic patterns and improvisation techniques.
  • Significance: The Mridangam is considered the "king of percussion instruments" in South Indian music and is essential for maintaining the tala (rhythmic cycle) in performances.

questions.question: Pandit Ram Narayan was associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.questionHtml: Pandit Ram Narayan was associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sarangi.

Key Points

  • Pandit Ram Narayan is a renowned musician who is credited with popularizing the Sarangi as a solo concert instrument in Hindustani classical music.
  • He was born on December 25, 1927, in Udaipur, Rajasthan, India.
  • Ram Narayan started his career as an accompanist for vocalists but later became a solo performer, showcasing the versatility and expressive capacity of the Sarangi.
  • He has received numerous awards and honors for his contribution to Indian classical music, including the Padma Vibhushan in 2005, one of India's highest civilian honors.

Additional Information

  • Sarangi
    • The Sarangi is a bowed, short-necked string instrument from the Indian subcontinent, used primarily in Hindustani classical music.
    • It is said to most resemble the sound of the human voice, able to imitate vocal ornaments such as gamaks (shakes) and meends (sliding movements).
    • The Sarangi is typically played while sitting cross-legged, with the instrument held vertically in front of the player.
    • The instrument is played with a bow, and the main strings are stopped with the cuticles or nails of the left hand, while the other fingers are used to modulate the pitch and resonance.
  • Rudra Veena
    • The Rudra Veena is a large plucked string instrument used in Hindustani classical music.
    • It is considered one of the most ancient and revered instruments in Indian music.
    • The instrument consists of a long tubular body with two large resonating gourds at either end.
  • Sarod
    • The Sarod is another prominent string instrument used in Hindustani classical music.
    • It is known for its deep, weighty, introspective sound and is used both for solo performances and as an accompaniment.
    • The Sarod is played with a plectrum, and the strings are stopped with the nails of the left hand.
  • Mohan Veena
    • The Mohan Veena is a modified slide guitar used in Indian classical music.
    • It was popularized by Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt, who won a Grammy Award for his performance with Ry Cooder in "A Meeting by the River".
    • The instrument is played with a slide, and it combines techniques and sounds from both Indian and Western musical traditions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a percussion instrument?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sarod.

Key Points

  • In percussion, the sound is produced by striking the animal skin which has been stretched across an earthen or metal pot or a wooden barrel or frame.
  • The main categories are-
    • Oordhwaka,
    • Ankya,
    • Alingya, and
    • the waisted or the Damaru family of drums

Additional Information

  • Tabla pair is a set of two vertical Oordhwaka drums.
  • Ankya drums are held horizontally before the musician and usually, both sides are covered with animal hide.
  • Oordhwaka drums are placed vertically before the musician and sound is produced by striking them with sticks or fingers.
  • Alingya drums have the animal hide fixed to a wooden round frame and are embraced or held close to the body with one hand while the other hand is used for playing the instrument.
  • Damru family is also known as the hourglass variety of drums as their shape resembles an hourglass.

questions.question: Umayalpuram K Sivaraman is an eminent musician associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.questionHtml: Umayalpuram K Sivaraman is an eminent musician associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mridangam.

Key Points

  • Umayalpuram K Sivaraman is a renowned Indian percussionist, known for his contributions to Carnatic music.
  • He is specifically famous for his mastery over the Mridangam, a traditional South Indian drum.
  • He has received numerous awards and honors, including the Padma Vibhushan, the second-highest civilian award in India, for his contributions to the field of music.
  • He has performed in various prestigious music festivals and has collaborated with many other eminent musicians both within India and internationally.

Additional Information

  • Mridangam
    • The Mridangam is a traditional double-headed drum used in South Indian classical music, known as Carnatic music.
    • It is made from a hollow piece of jackfruit wood, and its two drumheads are made from goat or cow skin.
    • The right head produces a high-pitched sound, while the left head produces a low-pitched sound, and the drum is played using both hands.
    • The Mridangam plays a crucial role in the rhythm section of Carnatic music ensembles, providing intricate rhythmic patterns and beats to accompany vocal and instrumental performances.
  • Sitar
    • The Sitar is a plucked string instrument used in Hindustani classical music, primarily in North India.
    • It has a long, hollow neck and a gourd body, with a varying number of strings, typically ranging from 18 to 20.
    • The Sitar is known for its distinctive sound, produced by plucking the strings with a metallic plectrum called a mizrab.
  • Guitar
    • The Guitar is a versatile string instrument used in various musical genres worldwide, including Western classical, rock, jazz, and folk music.
    • It usually has six strings, although there are variations with different numbers of strings.
    • The Guitar can be played by strumming or plucking the strings, and it is often used for both rhythm and lead parts in music.
  • Dhol

questions.question: __________ is often touted as Tansen of the 20 th century, this musical genius blended the best of classical music and created a unique style of his own.
questions.questionHtml: __________ is often touted as Tansen of the 20<sup>th</sup> century, this musical genius blended the best of classical music and created a unique style of his own.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bade Ghulam Ali Khan.

Key Points

  • Bade Ghulam Ali Khan was an iconic Indian classical vocalist from the Patiala Gharana.
  • He is often regarded as one of the greatest classical singers of the 20th century.
  • His unique style blended the best elements of classical music, creating a distinct sound that earned him immense respect and popularity.
  • He was known for his rich voice, intricate phrasing, and the ability to convey deep emotions through his music.

Additional Information

  • Patiala Gharana
    • The Patiala Gharana is one of the prominent schools of Indian classical music, known for its rich and elaborate style of singing.
    • It was founded in the mid-19th century by Fateh Ali Khan and Ali Baksh Khan.
    • The gharana is known for its intricate and swift taans (rapid melodic passages) and bol-baant (word division).
    • It has produced many eminent musicians, with Bade Ghulam Ali Khan being one of its most celebrated exponents.
  • Classical Music in India
    • Indian classical music is one of the oldest musical traditions in the world.
    • There are two main traditions: Hindustani classical music from North India and Carnatic classical music from South India.
    • Hindustani music focuses on the improvisational nature of ragas and is often performed in a more elaborate manner.
    • Carnatic music is known for its structured and composed nature, with a greater emphasis on kritis (compositions).
  • Raga
    • A raga is a melodic framework used in Indian classical music.
    • It is based on a specific scale and set of rules that guide the notes and motifs that can be used.
    • Each raga is associated with a particular time of day, season, mood, or emotion, and is intended to evoke specific feelings in the listener.
  • Vocal Techniques in Indian Classical Music
    • Indian classical vocal music employs various techniques such as alap (slow, improvisational introduction), jor (intermediate tempo), and jhala (fast-paced conclusion).
    • The use of taans (rapid melodic passages) and gamakas (ornamentations) adds complexity and beauty to the performance.
    • Singers often use a variety of rhythmic patterns and improvisations to showcase their skill and creativity.

questions.question: Which of the following is a cyclic arrangement of time units in Hindustani classical music?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a cyclic arrangement of time units in Hindustani classical music?
questions.solution: Tala is a fundamental concept in Hindustani classical music, representing a cyclic arrangement of time units that form the rhythmic framework for performances. Each tala consists of a specific number of beats, called matras, grouped into vibhags (sections). Common talas include Teentaal, Ektaal, and Jhaptaal. The tala system is crucial for both composition and improvisation, guiding timing and rhythm. Hindustani classical music emphasizes improvisation within the structured frameworks of raga (melodic) and tala (rhythmic), and it has a rich history influenced by various cultural and historical factors, including Persian and Mughal traditions.

questions.question: Which of the following Hindustani musical Gharanas is the oldest among all the Khayal Gayaki styles?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following Hindustani musical Gharanas is the oldest among all the Khayal Gayaki styles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gwalior Gharana.

Key Points

  • Gwalior Gharana
    • One of the oldest Khyal Gharanas of the Hindustani musical Gharanas is the Gwalior Gharana.
    • The great Mughal emperor Akbar's rule marked the beginning of the rise of Gwalior Gharana's.
    • The favorite vocalists of patrons of the arts, including Miyan Tansen, who ranked first among the court's vocalists, were from the town of Gwalior.
    • Naththan Khan, Naththan Pir Bakhsh, and his grandsons Haddu, Hassu, and Natthu Khan were some of the earliest masters (ustad) of this gharana.
    • Bade Mohammad Khan, known for his taan bazi style, was the chief musician in the royal court. 
    • The simplicity of the gharana is one of its defining characteristics, and one way to do this is through the use of well-known ragas, which save the listener from the trouble of trying to figure out the raga.

Additional Information

  • Agra Gharana
    • The Nauhar Bani is the ancestor of the Agra gharana, a tradition of Hindustani classical vocal music.
    • Khayal gayaki and Dhrupad-Dhamar are combined to create the gayaki of the Agra Gharana.
    • Both the khayal and dhrupad components are taught together in training rather than separately. T
    • The Agra Gharana of music was founded by Haji Sujan Singh. 
  • Kirana Gharana
    • The Kirana gharana laid more focus on melody than rhythm. 
    • It was founded by pioneer Abdul Karim Khan.
    • According to the way that Bhimshen Joshi blends virtuosity and melody, he has grown to be the most well-known musician in this gharana.
  • Atrauli Gharana
    • Ustad Alladiya Khan founded the Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana in the late 19th century.
    • This gharana, which emerged from the dhrupad lineage but is noted for khayal, produced renowned artists like Kesarbai Kerkar, Laxmibai Jadhav, Mogubai Kurdikar, Mallikarjun Mansur, Shruti Sadolikar, and Dhondutai Kulkarni. 
    • This gharana  gained a reputation for its distinctive vocal aesthetics, raga repertory, and technical skill.
